gaps.sentence: It's so quiet here — there's hardly ___ around.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' is a negative adverb, so it combines with 'anybody' (hardly anybody = almost nobody); 'nobody' would double the negative.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.

gaps.sentence: Have we got ___ eggs for breakfast?
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in neutral questions; 'none' cannot stand before a noun.
'Too cold to swim' means the temperature prevents swimming; 'enough' would follow the adjective.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: He was driving ___ fast for the icy road.
gaps.explanation: 'Too fast for something' means faster than is safe; 'so fast' needs a 'that' clause, not 'for'.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ point in complaining — no one will listen.
gaps.hint: fixed expression: ___ point in doing something
gaps.explanation: 'There's little point in doing something' means it is hardly worth doing; 'point' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: If you walk instead of driving, you'll spend ___ on petrol.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend less' is the comparative with uncountable money; 'fewer' is for countable nouns.
